notes.why: They were computed as total_runs / SUM(job seconds). A target's jobs run concurrently, so that is per-worker throughput, while the exec count beside it is a true cross-job total. Comparing the two implied 9-88 hours of work for a two-hour slice on 10 of 46 targets. ratchet.py now takes MAX(seconds) -- wall clock -- so new rates are ~jobs-times higher and no longer comparable to the old floors. Keeping them would make the rate ratchet pass trivially forever, which is worse than having none.

reseeds.reason: D1 fixed protocol_fuzzer to consume whole protocol messages instead of one byte per input. The old floors were earned while it was broken: enormous throughput at cov 380. Post-fix it does fewer executions at cov 4077 because each input now does real parsing. Ratcheting against the broken number would demand the bug back.
